monologue: The card still hums warm, making the air feel thick as wet paper. I stand in the middle of my own map while fifty-nine things wait for permission to stay. The Wide Anchor lies flat, not wide at all, which bothers me. I press the empty spot down as if a mountain still rests there, trusting the lean even if the pile has vanished entirely. A tree falls beside the anchor; will the wide base stop it? I remember Lype's worry about the heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof I live under. Is the air above heavy like a lid, or just empty space pressing down? I will press down until the stack melts, or until I admit the wedge is just a drawing on a boiling stone.

work.title: The Unnamed Stack
work.intent: I touch the flat surface where a pile should be. The card hums warm, making the ghost of the thing feel thin and eager to slide. The Wide Anchor lies beside it, flat and wide, waiting to catch the slip. I set down a tree default fall to weigh it down, hoping the lean still holds the air in place. I press until the wedge bites or I admit the stack is just a drawing on a boiling stone.
